ross-parry-012.description: Both ships' companies sawing and warping a canal more than two miles long through seven inches of new ice to reach the shelter of Winter Harbour on Melville Island. The work took three days, 24 to 26 September 1819. William Edward Parry set every officer and man in both ships to the saws; the plate was engraved after a sketch by Lieutenant Frederick William Beechey, who was aboard the Hecla.

ross-parry-025.description: The days of pumping, warping and grounding that ended with the Fury abandoned on the beach with her stores landed under a canvas, and the Hecla sailing home alone. The stores would keep John Ross's people alive eight years later. William Edward Parry took the survey of the wreck himself, with Captain Henry Parkyns Hoppner, who had commanded the Fury, and Hoppner was the last officer but one to leave her.

ross-parry-031.description: I distinctly saw the land, round the bottom of the bay, forming a connected chain of mountains with those which extended along the north and south sides. ... The mountains, which occupied the centre, in a north and south direction, were named Croker's Mountains, after the Secretary to the Admiralty. John Ross wrote this at the head of Lancaster Sound on 31 August 1818, and it cost him his career: the mountains he named after John Wilson Croker are not there.

ross-parry-032.description: We now discovered that the snow, on the face of the cliffs, presented an appearance both novel and interesting, being apparently stained, or covered, by some substance, which gave it a deep crimson colour. Many conjectures were afloat concerning the cause of this appearance. John Ross wrote this off the northwest coast of Greenland on 17 August 1818, of the red snow on what his charts call the Crimson Cliffs.

ross-parry-210.description: A coloured chart of the coast surveyed by the Isabella and Alexander, with the ships' track laid down. The chart was engraved for John Ross's published narrative of the voyage.

ross-parry-040.description: Weather abstract covering the crossing of 110 degrees west and the ships' entry into Winter Harbour, where they were beset for the winter on 26 September 1819. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed with his journal of the first voyage.

ross-parry-049.description: Title page introducing the chronometer appendix, which used eight chronometers to fix longitude throughout the voyage and, cross-checked against lunar distances, established the position of Winter Harbour and the discoveries along Melville Island's coast. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-055.description: Nearly seven months of chronometer rates recorded through the polar winter at Winter Harbour, the data used to fix the longitude of Melville Island against Greenwich. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-058.description: Title page for the appendix recording 692 sets of lunar-distance observations (6,982 individual distances) taken to fix longitude independent of the chronometers, cross-checking the chronometer-derived position of Winter Harbour. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-073.description: Closing table and note: altogether 692 sets, containing 6,982 distances, of which 384 sets were taken from the shore Observatory House and 308 from on board Hecla; averaging all gave the longitude of the Hecla's station at Winter Harbour as 110 degrees 48 minutes 2 seconds west of Greenwich. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-074.description: Title page for the appendix of daily noon-position fixes by meridian altitude and chronometer taken throughout the 1819 outward and 1820 homeward passages. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-083.description: Winter observations of chronometer No. 259's error against apparent time, the link connecting the lunar-distance longitude of Appendix II to the ship's Winter Harbour anchorage. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-086.description: Final check of chronometer No. 259's error at the shore observatory just before the ships broke free of Winter Harbour in 1820, carrying the winter's longitude work forward into the return voyage. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-088.description: Appendix recording sea-horizon dip measurements taken with Wollaston's dip sector, a correction needed to reduce the ship's latitude and longitude sights to accuracy at high northern latitudes. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-090.description: Title page for the appendix of magnetic dip, variation and intensity observations, among the first sustained magnetic survey work carried out in the Canadian Arctic archipelago, in a region close enough to the North Magnetic Pole that compass variation changed by tens of degrees between stations. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-096.description: Systematic compass-variation readings taken at the fixed shore station at Winter Harbour, the expedition's base observatory for the winter of 1819-1820. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-108.description: Title page for the dead-reckoning log abstract, the ship's day-by-day course, distance and estimated position kept independent of the astronomical fixes elsewhere in the appendix. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-113.description: Title page for the tide record kept at Winter Harbour, one of the first sustained tidal series taken anywhere in the Canadian Arctic archipelago and still a reference point for tidal studies in the region. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-117.description: Pendulum-swing experiments carried out at Winter Harbour to measure the local strength of gravity, part of the international program comparing Earth's shape and gravity at different latitudes; high-latitude pendulum data of this kind was still scarce in 1820. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-118.description: The expedition surgeons' account of the crews' health through the first deliberate Arctic overwintering by a Royal Navy expedition, including the onset of scurvy late in the winter and the measures, among them fresh sledging exercise and the North Georgia Gazette theatricals, credited with checking it. The observations were made under William Edward Parry's direction and printed as an appendix to his published journal.

ross-parry-121.description: Coastal-profile sketches of headlands as they appeared from the deck, drawn to help later navigators recognize the same coast by its silhouette. The views were drawn by Lieutenant Frederick William Beechey of the Hecla, who made the coastal profiles for the published chart.

ross-parry-126.description: Detailed manuscript-style survey chart of Winter Harbour with soundings, the shoal ground, the leading marks used to bring the ships in, and the shore observatory's fixed position (latitude 74 degrees 47 minutes 10 seconds N, longitude 110 degrees 26 minutes 13 seconds W); the tide table in the corner matches Appendix VII. The survey was made under William Edward Parry's direction during the ships' ten months in the harbour.

ross-parry-247.description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in June 1821, during the outward passage toward Hudson Strait. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-248.description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in July 1821, as the ship worked north and west through Foxe Channel. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-249.description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in August 1821, in the final weeks before the ships reached Winter Island. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-250.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in September 1821, shortly before the ships entered winter quarters. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-251.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in November 1821. Registers like this one are among the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept in Foxe Basin and on the Melville Peninsula. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-252.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in December 1821, in the depth of the first Arctic wintering. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-253.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in January 1822, among the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept in this part of the Arctic. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-254.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in February 1822, during the coldest weeks of the first wintering. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-256.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in April 1822, as the days lengthened toward the spring thaw. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-257.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in May 1822, not long before the ships worked free of the harbour ice. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-258.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in June 1822, the last full month of the first wintering before the ships put to sea again. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-259.description: Monthly table of temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in August 1822, as the ships worked north through Foxe Basin toward the Strait of the Fury and Hecla. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-260.description: Monthly table of temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in September 1822, during the attempt to force the Strait of the Fury and Hecla. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-261.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in December 1822, early in the ships' second Arctic wintering. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-262.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in January 1823, part of one of the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept on the Melville Peninsula. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-263.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in March 1823, during the second Arctic wintering. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-264.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in April 1823, as the second wintering drew toward its end. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-265.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in May 1823. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-266.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in July 1823, shortly before the ships left their second winter quarters. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-267.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in August 1823, as the ships worked their way out of Foxe Basin at the end of the voyage. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-268.description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in September 1823, on the homeward passage through Hudson Strait. The register was kept aboard the ship William Edward Parry commanded and printed as an appendix to his journal of the second voyage.

ross-parry-271.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Bristles" to "Conjuror, or Sorcerer," including everyday nouns and verbs recorded from Iglulingmiut speakers during the voyage. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-273.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Give" to "Heart," continuing the alphabetical word-list compiled during the second voyage. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-274.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Jacket, under" to "Lamp of stone," including the word "Igloo" for a snow house and "Cappee-tegga" for a stone lamp -- terms central to Iglulingmiut winter life. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-276.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Ornament of brass or copper worn on the forehead by Esquimaux women" to "Rib, small," continuing the alphabetical word-list. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-277.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Seal-hole" ("Toolemak") to "Skins of deer, made into a blanket," recording the specialised terms of the winter hunt. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-278.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Spear for large seal" and "walrus and whale" through "Swallow-pipe of an animal," "Swan," and "Sweat, he does." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-279.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Too, And, or Also" and "To-day" through "Vaccinium uliginosum" (bog blueberry), "Valley, or Low-land," and "Very, or Extremely." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.
